symptoms.potential_symptom: Frontend service failing RPC calls to search: gRPC Unavailable ('there is no connection available') indicating frontend cannot establish connections to search
symptoms.evidence: 20 error traces (sample traceIDs: 10b3de61c9fa020a, 5bb786ffbfd2cb6c, 7f9627dd998872d6) all show has_error=true and error_message='rpc error: code = Unavailable desc = there is no connection available' with sequence 'frontend -> search'. Reported latencies are small (~0.33–0.73 ms), consistent with immediate connection failures rather than timeouts.

rca_tasks.investigation_goal: Epicenter check: confirm frontend pods are healthy, inspect frontend gRPC client configuration (target hostname/port, connection pool settings) and immediate client-side error logs to verify the failures originate in the frontend process (app-domain hypothesis: frontend gRPC client misconfiguration or exhausted connections).

Connection check (two-sided): discover what downstream services frontend calls, then explicitly verify frontend's configured search address/port and compare to the Kubernetes service definition for search (dependency/config hypothesis: frontend is pointing at the wrong service name/port or using the wrong protocol).

Search-side check: verify search service has healthy endpoints/pods, inspect search pod container ports and recent logs for server startup/listen errors or crashes (app hypothesis: search has no ready gRPC server / crashed, causing frontend's 'no connection available').

Platform / network check: if search pods look healthy and frontend config matches service, snapshot cluster topology and enumerate platform dependencies (service-mesh, DNS, kube-proxy) that could block pod-to-pod connections (platform hypothesis: networking/mesh sidecar or cluster-level routing is preventing connections).

final_report.root_cause: Frontend gRPC client is resolving/targeting service-discovery names (e.g. 'srv-search') that do not yield usable backend addresses in-cluster, so the gRPC client never establishes sub-connections and immediately fails RPCs with 'rpc error: code = Unavailable desc = there is no connection available'. Concretely, the frontend binary/instance is using Consul-style service-discovery identifiers (printed as 'srv-search' in its startup logs) while the cluster routing observed is via the Kubernetes Service named 'search' (ClusterIP + endpoints). This name/resolution mismatch (or lack of the expected Consul SRV DNS answers to the gRPC resolver) results in the frontend having no READY subconn to the search server even though the search pod and Kubernetes Service are healthy and the search process registered with Consul.
final_report.evidence_summary: 1) Traces (20 samples) show immediate gRPC failures from frontend -> search with error 'rpc error: code = Unavailable desc = there is no connection available' and short latencies (~0.33–0.73 ms), indicating immediate connection resolution/failures rather than RPC timeouts. 2) Frontend pod (frontend-7fc7ddc9db-j2mk6) is Running/Ready with no ERROR/WARN logs or restarts; its logs show it initializes gRPC clients and prints service-discovery targets as 'srv-search', 'srv-profile', etc., and reads consul:8500 as Consul address. 3) Kubernetes Service 'search' exists (ClusterIP 10.96.101.64) on port 8082 with endpoints pointing to the running search pod. 4) Search pod (search-5c64c8f5bc-kzvjd) is Running and its logs show it started and 'Successfully registered in consul' with target port 8082, i.e., the search server is up and has endpoints. 5) Namespace snapshot shows a consul pod present (possible Consul-based discovery/mesh). Combined, these show the backend is healthy but the frontend's resolver/target naming (srv- prefixed) is not resulting in usable addresses for the gRPC client, producing the observed 'no connection available' failures.
final_report.investigation_summary: Priority-driven checks completed: (P1) Verified frontend pod health and logs; frontend shows no client-side errors but uses service-discovery names (srv-*) and points at consul:8500. (P2) Compared frontend dependency to Kubernetes Service 'search' — service exists and has endpoints; no manifest-level mismatch found. (P3) Verified search pod and logs — search gRPC server is running and registered in Consul. (P4) Examined namespace-level platform components — no Istio/Linkerd mesh detected; Consul is present and is the only namespace-level discovery component. Correlation: healthy backend + healthy frontend process but frontend RPCs failing immediately => failure in name resolution or resolver integration (service-discovery mismatch). The most likely causal chain: frontend configured to use Consul-style SRV names (srv-search) -> gRPC resolver obtains no usable addresses (Consul DNS/SRV not available to resolver or names mismatch) -> gRPC has no subchannel connections -> RPCs return Unavailable 'no connection available'.
